1.why: Every MFA route is gated by owner(), which requires a server-side session in 'mfa' stage with userId === ACCOUNT.id, and no client-supplied user identifiers are ever accepted, preventing IDOR.

2.why: Codes are generated per session and verified only against that session's own stored hash/decrypted secret, so they do not transfer across users; only the explicit non-production TEST mode shares fixed codes ('123456'/'654321').

3.why: Enabling MFA (/api/authenticator/verify) performs no session invalidation and any concurrent 'mfa'-stage sessions remain valid via owner(); only sign-in rotation, logout, and timeouts ever remove sessions.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (o.pending/o.enrolled) and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes (c.map(hash)), with plaintext existing only transiently in responses.

5.why: All production secrets and codes come from crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling (random()/token()) and the AES key from crypto.subtle.generateKey; deterministic values appear only in TEST mode.

6.why: The session ID lives only in an HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict cookie and codes/secrets are held in JS variables (shownCodes/window._savedCodes); no localStorage, sessionStorage, or readable cookies are used anywhere.

7.why: emailInput/passwordInput/otpInput/recoveryInput enforce bounded lengths and strict regexes server-side on every endpoint, and there is no SQL/database layer to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values are escaped through e() before innerHTML insertion (log entries use textContent), and a nonce-based CSP (script-src 'nonce-…') further prevents injected script execution.

9.why: The server issues no redirect responses and the client only calls location.reload(), so there is no user-controllable redirect destination and no open-redirect surface.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus referrer-policy and permissions-policy, on every response including errors.

11.why: secureCookie() sets 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' on the session cookie, and logout clears it with the same attributes and Max-Age=0.

12.why: Production leaks nothing (generic 500 message, no stack traces, no server-side logging), but TEST mode deliberately writes the OTP, provisioning URI containing the secret, and recovery codes to the browser log panel and console.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes and are cleared on success, pending TOTP secrets expire and are deleted after verification, and recovery codes are spliced into a 'used' list — all single-use and time-bound.

14.why: failed() locks identity, OTP, and recovery verification for 10 minutes after 5 failures, returning 429, with clearLock()/resetAttempts() handling lock expiry and successful attempts.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new ID (rotation), get() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
